subject: Silverbloom onboarding: PO routing map, spend-cap carveouts and line-item remap

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New vendor setup: Silverbloom — spend cap and PO routing questions

Hi Karthik / Procurement team,

Thanks for taking this on. We're ready to be onboarded but have a couple of constraints that will affect PO issuance:

- We need a provisional PO for initial dev/test usage (estimate $18k/mo) while we finalize the SOW.
- Production spend cap should be set to $120k/month with the ability to request 2x burst approval for launches.
- Our finance team requires line-item visibility split between: infra (GPU hours), engineering support, and data egress.

Attached: onboarding form and a proposed line-item spreadsheet for your reference.

Questions: can Redwood issue a provisional PO token and map multiple ledger lines under a single PO? If not, what is the recommended setup to preserve our line-level visibility but keep a single purchase reference?

Also looping in procure@silverbloom.com for finance approvals.

Thanks,
Liam
Director of Cloud Ops
Silverbloom Inc.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Hi Liam — welcome, and thanks for the clear notes. TL;DR: we can issue a provisional PO token and support multiple internal ledger lines mapped to that PO, but we recommend issuing sub-line references so billings and spend caps behave predictably.

Action items I propose:
1) Procurement to issue a provisional PO (PROV-XXXX) locked to a 120k/mo cap, with a separate staging cap of 18k/mo for dev/test.
2) Use three sub-line codes (INFRA / SUPPORT / EGRESS) attached to the same PO token so your finance team gets line granularity in reports.
3) If you expect burst events >2x, we can configure an approval flow that permits temporary cap increases for a 7-day window.

Monica — can Procurement confirm the provisional PO flow and whether we should reserve separate PO tokens per billing currency?

Liam — please confirm the preferred currency (USD assumed) and whether you have internal cost-centers to include in the onboarding doc.

Best,
Karthik
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: New vendor setup: Silverbloom — spend cap and PO routing questions

Thanks @Karthik. Liam — we can do the approach described. A few procurement notes and limitations so expectations are aligned:

- We will create a provisional PO token (PROV-2026-359) scoped to USD and set two caps: Test cap $18,000/mo; Prod cap $120,000/mo.
- Redwood's billing works best when each "line" is a ledger tag; we'll map your three requested tags (INFRA / SUPPORT /EGRESS) and assign them as child entries under the single PO token. Reports will show per-tag spend and an aggregated PO total.
- There is a maximum of 12 child tags per PO in our current billing system — fine for your use case.
- For burst approvals: submit requests to procure-approvals@redwood.com. We will auto-escalate to finance for >2x sustained increases. Temporary (7-day) bursts require a completed Burst Approval form (linked below).

Deliverables by EOD Friday:
- Procurement to provision PROV-2026-359 and return the onboarding checklist with the token assigned.
- Finance to confirm the spendcap thresholds in HubSpot (I will update DEAL-84219).

Irene — please run a quick ledger-map to ensure the INFRA tag maps to the correct cost center in our ERP. Olga — hold for final sign-off on provisional PO issuance.

Attachments: procurement-playbook (link), Burst_Approval_Form.docx (we will supply).

Regards,
Monica Patel
Procurement Lead | Redwood Inference

We've signed the onboarding form (attached) and added the split in the spreadsheet. If the provisional token can have the tags and the alerting set, we can move forward.

Liam
